title: High Strength and Fracture Resistance of Reduced-Activity W-Ta-Ti-V-Zr High-Entropy Alloy for Fusion Energy Applications.

recollection.starting_material: W-Ta-Ti-V-Zr elemental powders or chunks melted together to form a W-Ta-Ti-V-Zr equiatomic high-entropy alloy (guess)
recollection.intervention: vacuum arc melting followed by hot forging or hot rolling and annealing to refine grains and homogenize the composition (guess)
recollection.structure: predominantly body‐centered cubic (BCC) solid‐solution matrix with nanoscale precipitates or fine‐grained structure on the order of 1–5 μm (guess)
recollection.mechanism: strengthening primarily via solid‐solution hardening and grain‐boundary strengthening, with possible secondary‐phase precipitation for crack‐tip blunting and improved fracture resistance (guess)
recollection.results: ultimate tensile strength around 1.2–1.4 GPa, yield strength ~1.0 GPa, fracture toughness ~25–30 MPa·m^1/2, and less than 10% residual radioactivity after neutron irradiation equivalent to a typical fusion first wall dose (guess)

score.note: The recollection correctly identifies arc melting, a BCC character, and solid-solution strengthening, but adds nonexistent forging/rolling/annealing, grain refinement, nanoscale precipitates, and precipitation/grain-boundary strengthening. It misses the segregated dual-BCC dendritic structure and the proposed roles of lattice distortion and Ti/V/Zr in plasticity and crack resistance. The strength and toughness estimates are not close to the reported ~1.6 GPa compressive yield strength, ~1.8 GPa ultimate compressive strength, and ~38 MPa√m toughness; the tensile and irradiation claims were not reported.
